limits: Survey with no new experiments; all numbers are reported from cited work and cut-off is mid-2023 (arXiv v1, 25 Jul 2023).
Excludes image generative models (GANs, VAEs, diffusion), explicitly out of scope (Sec 2.1).
Table 3 mixes results under different evaluation mechanisms (asterisked cells), so rows are not strictly comparable.
Authors concede GPT-4 is closed so open-source models cannot be matched on known details; evaluation of conversational VLMs lacks agreed benchmarks.
Retrieval-augmented generation is only named as a hallucination mitigation; no multimodal RAG, document-image or OCR pipeline coverage.
practices: Use handcrafted prompt templates such as 'A photo of a {label}' for CLIP-style zero-shot classification; added context helps (Sec 1, 2.4.3).
Convert one-word-label vision datasets to image-text training data with template prompts (Sec 2.4.3).
Bridge a frozen vision encoder to a frozen LLM with a light module (linear projection, Q-Former, Perceiver Resampler) to avoid costly end-to-end training (Sec 3.2, 3.3.1, 4).
Train in two stages: align the projection on image-caption pairs first, then instruction-tune on curated visual instruction data (MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, InstructBLIP; Sec 3.3.1, 4).
Make visual instruction data cheaply by prompting ChatGPT/GPT-4 for conversations, descriptions and reasoning (LLaVA, Sec 4).
Do not apply CLIP directly to localisation tasks; use region-text alignment, grounding pretraining or dense-feature adaptations (Sec 3.1.2).
Mask image tokens during contrastive training to cut compute 2-4x (FLIP) (Sec 3.1.1).
Adapt SAM to new domains by adapters, auxiliary prompt encoders or decoder-only fine-tuning rather than retraining (Sec 5.1.1).
To curb VLM hallucination, give explicit grounding instructions, use chain-of-thought, self-consistency voting, or retrieval from knowledge bases (Sec 8).
Use parameter-efficient adaptation (LoRA, QLoRA, prefix tuning, adapters) for FMs, with careful choice of rank and adapter placement (Sec 8).
Treat indirect prompt injection as a risk for LLM/VLM-integrated applications that retrieve external content (Sec 8).

terms.definition: the base models trained on large-scale data in a self-supervised or semi-supervised manner that can be adapted for several other downstream tasks
separate encoders process visual and textual modalities and their outputs are aligned by an objective function
adds a fusion encoder that takes vision and text representations and learns fused representations
an encoder-decoder language model plus a visual encoder
an LLM as the core component with a visual encoder converting images into a format compatible with the LLM
Image-Text Contrastive loss: match correct image-text pairs among N x N configurations, maximising cosine similarity of N correct pairs and minimising it among N^2-N incorrect pairs
Image-Text Matching: a few perceptron layers predict whether a pair is matched, trained with cross-entropy
treats the image as a prefix of the text description and reconstructs the remaining text given a prefix of random length
models steered by text (contrastive, generative, hybrid, conversational) versus by visual prompts such as boxes, points or masks (SAM, SegGPT)
output from a large VLM/LLM that is unreal or nonsensical; for VLMs includes ignoring the visual input and answering from the text prompt alone
